glassmere parity bench

The same scenarios, built three ways and driven with the same mouse and keyboard steps. The web column is Chromium, the engine behind Tauri's WebView2 on Windows; Qt is PySide6 with the Fusion style on the offscreen platform. Amber cells are where a column differs from the web.

Performance

A list of N rows (a label, a button and a check box each) in a 400 px scroll area. Each cell is first frame / one label changes / one scroll step, in milliseconds. The web number is main-thread time from the DevTools protocol (script, style, layout, recording the paint; raster runs on other threads and is not counted). Qt's is wall time to lay out and paint the visible part. glassmere's is a whole frame as a host runs it (messages, the view, reconcile, layout, paint) plus a full software raster. All on the same machine in one process, so read the ratios, not the digits.

toolkit100 rows1000 rows5000 rows
Web (Chromium, as in Tauri) plain DOM18.3 / 2.44 / 0.9249.9 / 4.68 / 1.39237 / 12.0 / 2.12
Qt (PySide6, Fusion) QWidget rows41.1 / 2.32 / 3.95208 / 4.35 / 4.601521 / 15.5 / 9.42
glassmere plain6.59 / 0.84 / 1.3368.8 / 8.03 / 10.9456 / 44.7 / 86.6
glassmere plain + Ui::memo6.35 / 0.61 / 0.7950.4 / 1.40 / 4.04343 / 6.60 / 38.4
glassmere virtual list2.22 / 0.62 / 0.902.64 / 0.61 / 0.832.31 / 0.60 / 0.83

How to read this

Observations come from the framework itself: Chromium's accessibility tree and :focus-visible, Qt's QAccessible, and glassmere's snapshots and scene. A pointer is reported as the framework would show it; for the web an auto cursor is read as an I-beam over text and the arrow elsewhere. Qt draws its focus frame from the style and cannot be asked, so its ring is not compared. Qt's first control takes focus when its window is shown, as in a real application. Qt Widgets has no switch, so the switch is a check box there.
